tools.name: search_entities
tools.summary: Search entities by name; the ONLY legitimate way to turn a name into ids.
tools.description:
Search entities by name; the ONLY legitimate way to turn a name into ids.

Always resolve names through this (or lookup_orcid) before using a
semantic_id — never guess ids. entity_type: one of authors, institutions,
sources, countries, subfields, or "all". Returns matches with semanticId,
papers, citations and a rankless_url backlink.

tools.name: get_top_entities
tools.summary: Top entities per type (institutions, authors, sources, countries, subfields).
tools.description:
Top entities per type (institutions, authors, sources, countries, subfields).

Good starting seeds when exploring without a specific target.

tools.name: get_entity_profile
tools.summary: Full profile of one entity: totals, yearly series, top relations, similars.
tools.description:
Full profile of one entity: totals, yearly series, top relations, similars.

`yearlyPapers`/`yearlyCites` cover the recent era (2016..now). `relations`
holds ranked related entities per relation type (paper-fields,
citing-fields, paper-journals, paper-authors, ...).

tools.name: get_entity_stats
tools.summary: Lifetime + year-windowed paper/citation counts, top citing subfields.
tools.description:
Lifetime + year-windowed paper/citation counts, top citing subfields.

The per-year window only covers the recent era (2016..now); `windowFrom`/
`windowTo` in the response show the clamped range actually used. Pass
`subfield` (a subfields semantic_id) for that subfield's citation slice.

tools.name: get_citation_tree
tools.summary: Hierarchical citation-impact breakdown of an entity, flattened to top-N.
tools.description:
Hierarchical citation-impact breakdown of an entity, flattened to top-N.

`tree_index` picks a breakdown config (see `levels` in the response for
what each level means); `since_year` is a single lower cutoff.
`citationLinks` counts citation links into a node, `sourceWorks` counts
the entity's own works under it.

tools.name: get_papers
tools.summary: Papers of an entity. sort="citations" ranks by citation count first.
tools.description:
Papers of an entity. sort="citations" ranks by citation count first.

Returns paper title, year, doi and citation count.

tools.name: get_peers
tools.summary: Peer entities (comparable size + field profile) and top subfields.
tools.description: Peer entities (comparable size + field profile) and top subfields.

tools.name: lookup_orcid
tools.summary: Resolve an ORCID iD (e.g. 0000-0001-7896-6217) to a rankless author.
tools.description: Resolve an ORCID iD (e.g. 0000-0001-7896-6217) to a rankless author.

foci.name: share
foci.description: genuinely interesting, TRUE, shareable findings: surprising rankings, striking trends, unexpected cross-field impact, David-vs-Goliath comparisons, human-interest angles. Classify each with `share_kind`: entity-value (spotlight one entity's standing), comparison (two+ entities), strengths-weaknesses (where an entity dominates vs lags), analysis (a deeper multi-number read), or other.

foci.name: query
foci.description: the result of a specific investigation. Report the answer plainly in `description`, set `question` to the exact question answered, and back it with metrics.

foci.name: data-issue
foci.description: possible data problems: implausible counts, duplicates, zeros, extreme outliers, wrong attributions, garbled/mojibake names, mismatched field/journal mappings. Set `issue_kind`: "ledger-fix" if a single logged-in user edit would correct it - then fill `ledger_suggestion` (kind one of merge_authors / merge_papers / claim_paper / disown_paper / add_paper_request, a human `note`, and any ids/names you can infer in `details`; omit ids you cannot see) - or "investigation" if it needs more digging first.

options.help: one of ['local', 'live'] or a full /v1 base URL (default: local).
comma list of ['share', 'query', 'data-issue'] or 'all' (default: query when --investigate/--question, else share).
center the round on one entity/scope, e.g. 'Hungary' or 'authors:balazs-lengyel'.
a specific investigation for the query focus.
deepen a past finding: '<run>' or '<run>:<id>' under the writeups dir.

resources.text:
# Rankless entity types

Root types (valid `entity_type` values): authors, institutions, sources,
countries, subfields.

- sources = journals/venues.
- subfields = the discipline level used everywhere (the UI calls them
  "Fields"); topics nest under subfields.
- semantic_id is the stable slug identifying an entity (e.g. authors/
  david-baker, institutions/nyu). Ids must come from search_entities /
  lookup_orcid — never guessed.
- citations are counted over the recent era (2016..now) unless stated
  otherwise; `papers` counts the full lifetime.

# Using the rankless tools

1. Resolve first: turn every name into a semantic_id via search_entities (or
   lookup_orcid). Disambiguate homonyms by papers/citations/distinctText.
2. Aggregate second: get_entity_profile / get_entity_stats / get_citation_tree
   / get_peers / get_papers over resolved ids.
3. Every response carries rankless_url backlinks - cite them so humans can
   verify.
4. All numbers are deterministic backend aggregates; the same call always
   returns the same value. Never invent or extrapolate numbers.
